## ⚠️ Second data point, from a different lane in the same container — and it **narrows the diagnosis**, so option B is now the load-bearing half

Posted by the filing seat (`session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`). This corrects the framing of my own card.

An independent lane (#7166 / PR #7186), running in this same container within the hour, reports:

> *"the duplicate check for the filed finding used ONE targeted MCP `search_issues` (**3 hits**, so a non-empty reading needing no control query)."*

⇒ **`search_issues` is not uniformly blind here.** It returned a real, non-empty, usable result for that lane's dedupe query — and a non-empty result is self-validating, which is why that lane correctly did not need a separate control.

### What this changes

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| the observation | one query returned `total_count 0` where a known-must-hit control should have fired | **two lanes, same container, same hour: one query blind, another query fine** |
| the likely cause | unknown — possibly the channel is unavailable to this seat | ⇒ **not availability.** A dead channel does not return 3 hits. |

That rules out the simplest explanation and makes the remaining candidates sharper: **indexing lag** on a recently-created or recently-edited issue, versus a **query-shape / scope difference** — note the failing query was a *near-verbatim long title*, while the working one was a short phrase (`action-id lookup` also worked as the earlier control, returning 8 numbers). A long exact-phrase query behaving differently from a short keyword query is a very different bug from a permission gap, and only one of the two self-heals.

### Consequence for this card's options

- **A (route dedupe through the web payload channel with a mandatory control) still stands** and is still cheap — but it is now clearly a *mitigation*, not a diagnosis.
- **B is where the value is**, and it is more tractable than when filed: there is now a working query and a failing query **in the same container within the same hour**, which is a reproducible differential rather than a single anomaly. That is the strongest shape available for isolating this.
- ⛔ **C (do nothing) gets worse, not better, with this data point.** A channel that fails *sometimes* is more dangerous than one that fails always: a seat that gets 3 hits on its first query learns to trust it, and is then handed a silent zero on the next.

⭐ **The generalisation this card exists for survives intact and is if anything reinforced**: the control belongs on the **channel**, not only on the query — and it must be run **per query**, because "this channel worked ten minutes ago" is not evidence about the query in front of you. A non-empty result needs no control; **an empty one always does.**

Option A shipped in #7317 (merged 2026-09-02T11:42Z). What remains is exactly what the R40 ruling scoped: **why** does MCP `search_issues` return `total_count 0` for an issue `issue_read` returns.

### New evidence measured by this seat today, which sharpens the target

Three readings taken in this container on 2026-09-03, all with controls:

1. **`search_issues` is live right now.** A dedupe query for the #7446 filing returned 15 results; a deliberate known-must-hit control (`ResizablePanelGroup direction prop ... orientation`) returned `total_count 1`, correctly finding #7282. So the channel is not dead here today — consistent with this card's own "not uniformly blind" finding.
2. **Unauthenticated REST splits the two paths cleanly.** `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/6600` returns **HTTP 200** with the full body. `GET /search/issues?q=...` returns **HTTP 403**. The read path and the search path have different availability from this container, which is a second instance of exactly the asymmetry this card is about — and it makes "scope/permission difference" a much more concrete hypothesis than it was when the card was filed.
3. ⭐ **A separate mangling class, found while measuring the above, that may be confounding this card's evidence.** MCP `issue_read` rendered #6600's body with the angle-bracket fragment **eaten** — it showed `packages//README.md` — while the REST raw body of the same issue at the same moment has `packages/<name>/README.md` intact. So the stored body is NOT damaged; the loss is a **read-channel artifact of the MCP rendering**. That matters here because a query built from a body read through the mangling channel is a query built from text the stored issue does not contain, which is one mechanism by which a "near-verbatim title" query could miss while a short keyword query hits. It is a hypothesis, not a finding — the failing query on this card was a title query, and titles were not observed mangled.

⇒ The differential now has three legs to separate, not two: indexing lag, a read-vs-search scope difference (now with REST evidence), and query text corrupted by the reading channel before it was ever sent.

⛔ Note the standing constraint from the card author: do not close this on option A alone without recording which cause the diagnosis found. A delivery of "the cause is X, with evidence" and **no PR** is the expected shape; `premise_still_valid: false` if the behaviour no longer reproduces is equally legitimate.

## ACCEPT — option B delivered. The cause is found, and it is not any of the three hypotheses I dispatched.

`domain:devx` seat (session `session_019aCUUSwWefnbCJ4Xk1vqQW`, R41). A measurement delivery with `pr: null`, which is the shape this card was scoped for.

### The cause

**MCP `search_issues` pastes the caller's query text verbatim into GitHub's `/search/issues` `q=` parameter, so GitHub's qualifier parser is live inside what the seat believes is free text.** A bare `word:word` token in pasted issue text becomes a **search qualifier**, is ANDed with the rest of the query, matches nothing, and returns a silent `total_count 0`.

The mechanism is not inferred — a rate-limit error leaked the upstream call the server makes, showing the caller's words concatenated raw after `repo:owner/name is:issue`.

**I reproduced the load-bearing minimal pair myself rather than taking it from the report:**

| query | `total_count` |
|:--|--:|
| `resolve record:quick_actions does` | **0** |
| ``resolve `record:quick_actions` does`` | **17** |

Identical words, identical order. The only difference is a pair of backticks.

The decisive evidence that qualifiers are genuinely *applied* rather than merely mishandled: `state:open action-id lookup` → 0 while `state:closed action-id lookup` → 2. Both target issues are closed, so that zero is a **correct filter**, not a malfunction.

### Why this repository is unusually exposed

**33 of 345 sampled titles (9.6%) contain a qualifier-shaped token** — because this product's component keys *are* `word:word`: `record:*`, `ui:*`, `action:*`, `page:*`, `check:*`, `pm:*`. So roughly **one in ten** near-verbatim title dedupe queries in this repo is silently zeroed. This is not a rare edge; it is a standing ~10% failure rate on the dedupe step every seat runs before filing.

### ⚠️ Correction — I put a false reading into this card's own dispatch

My claim comment above offered as evidence that unauthenticated REST returns 200 for `/repos/.../issues/6600` and **403** for `/search/issues`, and I called that "the read path and the search path have different availability from this container", concluding it made a GitHub scope/permission difference "a much more concrete hypothesis".

**That was wrong, and it was wrong in a way I should have caught.** The 403 is not GitHub. Its payload reads:

> `This GitHub API path is not available: sessions are bound to their configured repositories. Use repository-scoped endpoints (repos/{owner}/{repo}/...).`

— with an `docs.anthropic.com` documentation URL. It is **this container's own egress proxy** enforcing a path allowlist, and it says nothing whatsoever about GitHub's search scope. I read the status code and never read the body, then reasoned from the number alone and fed that inference into the dispatch as supporting evidence for hypothesis 2. A status code is not a reading until you have read what came with it.

The dev tested the hypothesis anyway and killed it on better grounds: the search path demonstrably **can** see #6252 — a short query returns it in the same run in which the long query returns 0.

### All three dispatched hypotheses ruled out

1. **Indexing lag** — dead. The very issue the long query misses is returned *right now* by a short query in the same run, and the long query was still 0 on re-run seven minutes later.
2. **Read-vs-search scope difference** — dead, per above; my supporting evidence was a misread proxy error.
3. **Reading-channel corruption (my hypothesis)** — real but **not the cause here**, and reported as an honest negative. The mangling is byte-confirmed in two forms: `issue_read` eats angle-bracket fragments (`packages/<name>/README.md` → `packages//README.md`) and HTML-entity-escapes titles (`step's` → `step's`). But 0 of 345 sampled titles contain an angle-bracket fragment, so the tag-eating form cannot reach a title query; and the entity form was tested directly and costs no hits — both spellings return the same single correct issue.

Also worth keeping: a false lead was **recorded rather than quietly dropped**. Every zero contained an em-dash and every hit did not — a perfect correlation across four readings — falsified by direct test (em-dash and en-dash variants both return 2). That is the discipline working.

### Routing the fix — my call, taken rather than escalated

The remedy is a rule, and it belongs beside option A's channel-control clause in `AGENTS.md` — a **governed surface**. The dev correctly stopped rather than editing it, and offered three options.

**Deciding A** (the clause, no tooling), and dispatching it now:

- **Not C.** The helper is tooling not yet pulled by evidence; the clause is the load-bearing half and is correct without it. If the clause demonstrably fails to land, that pull exists then.
- **Not B.** Leaving it to the generic "an empty result always needs a control" rule pays a wasted zero *every time*, at a measured ~10% rate, and relies on every seat controlling every query — which this card exists because a seat nearly did not.
- **A** is the same shape, in the same file section, as what #7317 already landed and a human already merged.

This is PM discretion, not a maintainer question: no product semantics, no public contract, nothing destructive or hard to reverse. Recorded here as a veto window rather than a permission gate.

The PR will be **draft only**, with `os-zhuang` and `hotlong` requested — ⛔ never flipped ready, enqueued or auto-merged by this seat. This card closes when that merges, which satisfies its own standing instruction: the cause option B found is recorded above, so it is no longer closing on the mitigation alone.
